entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please wait while we connect you to the next available agent.
Thank you for holding. My name is David. How can I help you today?
Hi David, I need to start a return for my VeloBand GPS tracker. It's not working correctly.
I'm certainly sorry to hear you're having trouble with it. To make sure I understand, what specifically is the issue? Is it a technical fault or more of a preference issue?
It's a technical fault. The GPS tracking is completely off. It said my 5-mile run was only 2 miles. For what I paid, this thing is a piece of garbage.

I can definitely understand your frustration with inaccurate tracking. That's the primary function, and it needs to be reliable. I can absolutely help with this. The first step for a potential defect is to connect you with our technical support team. They can run a remote diagnostic and see what's going on.
No, I don't want to do that. I don't have time for a long troubleshooting call. I just want a refund.

I appreciate that you want a fast solution. In order for me to process a return based on a defect, our policy requires that we first verify the fault. Without that verification, I have to handle it as a standard return, which is based on the purchase date.
Look, I'm not interested in being a beta tester for your product. It's broken. I just want money back for an item that doesn't work as advertised.

I understand your position. Let me pull up your account to check the policy details for your specific order. One moment... Okay, I see you purchased the VeloBand Pulse, and it was delivered 14 days ago, on January 3rd.

Okay. So, for the VeloBand Pulse model specifically, due to the way the hardware activates and links to a user's health data, we have a strict 10-day return window. Since you are on day 14, a return for a refund is no longer an option according to policy.
I see. 10 days is a very short window. Given that it's defective and I'm only four days over, can't you make an exception? How about a partial credit?

I'm afraid the 10-day window for the Pulse is a hard stop in our system, so I can't process any kind of refund. However, your one-year manufacturer's warranty is fully active. The best path forward is to let me transfer you to technical support. If they confirm the defect, they will ship you a brand new replacement unit at no cost.

A replacement of the same model doesn't really help if there's a fundamental issue. What about a store credit I can use for something else? Or maybe a significant discount code for a future purchase, as a gesture of goodwill?

I appreciate you trying to find a compromise. Unfortunately, my system won't allow me to issue credits or discounts for this situation once it's past the 10-day mark. The policy is really built around the warranty, so troubleshooting and replacement is the only option I'm authorized to provide.

Alright, David. It sounds like your hands are tied. It's a frustrating policy, but I understand you have to follow it. I'll think about whether I want to bother with the tech support call. Thanks for your time.

You're very welcome, and I'm sorry we couldn't reach a different outcome today. Please do call back if you decide you'd like to proceed with the warranty claim. We're here to help. Have a good rest of your day.
